accuracy.evidence: Every lab number is computed live from the stated rates: 24.9% APR gives a 1.8701% monthly rate, £1,000 grows to £1,948 in 36 months versus £1,747 simple, and £1,500 on interest plus 1% (or £5) takes 272 months and £2,590 interest. Loan totals use the annuity formula (£99.92 x 36, £78.73 x 84). Plan 5 terms (9% above £25,000, RPI interest, 40-year write-off) follow the Student Loans Company guidance; BNPL regulation follows the FCA July 2026 rules.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented money slips: judging a loan by the monthly payment (Loan B feedback states it costs £3,016 more), treating the minimum payment as a plan, believing pay in 3 is not real credit, reading Plan 5 as an ordinary debt where owing more means paying more, and expecting simple rather than compound growth on an unpaid card balance.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdebt is the only lab built on borrowing maths: a month slider that draws compound against simple-interest curves, five payment chips that overlay balance-over-time payoff curves, two loan cards with hidden totals and a draggable tick, a BNPL basket feeding three instalment bars against a budget line, and a salary bar split at the Plan 5 threshold. The shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each conclusion is reached by doing: the learner watches the red curve pull away from the dashed line, sees the minimum curve crawl along for 22 years next to the £100 curve, finds Loan B's total only after tapping, watches next month's bar cross the £50 line on the third buy, and switches the debt size to see the repayment stay put.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: £1,747 (24.9% three times) against about £1,950, About 3 years against Over 20 years for the minimum payment, and £2,700 (9% of the whole salary) against £450 for a £30,000 Plan 5 salary. The following task tests each guess and the done message names it.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own reason: APR confused with the monthly payment or credit limit, minimum and low fixed payments with their real interest cost, Loan B chosen on monthly cost, pay in 3 treated as not credit, Plan 5 tied to the amount owed or the rate, and compound growth blamed on fees or a rising APR.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK 3.4 against the learner limit of 6.5, with one term defined per sentence and a worked figure in each paragraph. Adult text scores FK 6.6 against 9.5 and uses the curriculum terms credit, debt, principal, interest, APR, compound interest, minimum repayment, overdraft, credit file and deferred payment credit.

no_filler.evidence: No stock phrases; the filler gate passed. Kid paragraphs define the terms with real figures; adult paragraphs give curriculum placement, how each lab figure was modelled, the four common mistakes including the Plan 5 misreading, and what the lab does. The explanation overlaps other lessons by under 12%.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark show a full-width month slider, five payment chips across the top, stacked loan cards with a 44 px tick, four item cards in one row above the bars, and a salary slider. Pointer tests dragged both sliders, tapped chips and cards, dragged the tick onto each loan and dragged items into the basket.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs axe run found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme on desktop or iPhone. Every canvas action has a labelled button: +6 months, five payment buttons, reveal and choose for each loan, one buy button per item, three salary presets and a loan switch. The canvas aria-label reads each result, including slider results on release.
